claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 faithfully captures the introductory mandate of 40 CFR 262.11 requiring a person generating solid waste (defined in 40 CFR 261.2) to make an accurate hazardous waste determination to ensure proper management under RCRA regulations. All dimensions are properly aligned with the source.

source_spans.quote:
A person who generates a solid waste, as defined in 40 CFR 261.2, must make an accurate determination as to whether that waste is a hazardous waste in order to ensure wastes are properly managed according to applicable RCRA regulations. A hazardous waste determination is made using the following steps:

(a) The hazardous waste determination for each solid waste must be made at the point of waste generation, before any dilution, mixing, or other alteration of the waste occurs, and at any time in the course of its management that it has, or may have, changed its properties as a result of exposure to the environment or other factors that may change the properties of the waste such that the RCRA classification of the waste may change.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0001 reproduces the requirement in paragraph (a) regarding timing and conditions for making the hazardous waste determination: at the point of waste generation before alteration, and at any time during management if properties may have changed. The passive construction and scope accurately reflect the source.

source_spans.quote: A person who generates a solid waste, as defined in 40 CFR 261.2, must make an accurate determination as to whether that waste is a hazardous waste in order to ensure wastes are properly managed according to applicable RCRA regulations. A hazardous waste determination is made using the following steps:
(b) A person must determine whether the solid waste is excluded from regulation under 40 CFR 261.4.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0002 accurately extracts paragraph (b), requiring a determination of whether the solid waste is excluded under 40 CFR 261.4. The actor, modality, and reference to 261.4 are correct and supported.

source_spans.quote: A person who generates a solid waste, as defined in 40 CFR 261.2, must make an accurate determination as to whether that waste is a hazardous waste in order to ensure wastes are properly managed according to applicable RCRA regulations. A hazardous waste determination is made using the following steps:

(c) If the waste is not excluded under 40 CFR 261.4, the person must then use knowledge of the waste to determine whether the waste meets any of the listing descriptions under subpart D of 40 CFR part 261. Acceptable knowledge that may be used in making an accurate determination as to whether the waste is listed may include waste origin, composition, the process producing the waste, feedstock, and other reliable and relevant information. If the waste is listed, the person may file a delisting petition under 40 CFR 260.20 and 260.22 to demonstrate to the Administrator that the waste from this particular site or operation is not a hazardous waste.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0003 correctly conveys the requirement in the first sentence of paragraph (c) to use knowledge of the waste to determine if it meets listing descriptions under subpart D of 40 CFR part 261, conditionally upon the waste not being excluded under 40 CFR 261.4.

A hazardous waste determination is made using the following steps:

(c) If the waste is not excluded under 40 CFR 261.4, the person must then use knowledge of the waste to determine whether the waste meets any of the listing descriptions under subpart D of 40 CFR part 261. Acceptable knowledge that may be used in making an accurate determination as to whether the waste is listed may include waste origin, composition, the process producing the waste, feedstock, and other reliable and relevant information. If the waste is listed, the person may file a delisting petition under 40 CFR 260.20 and 260.22 to demonstrate to the Administrator that the waste from this particular site or operation is not a hazardous waste.

claim_judgments.rationale: In § 262.11(c), the permission to file a delisting petition under 40 CFR 260.20 and 260.22 is governed by the paragraph lead-in condition ('If the waste is not excluded under 40 CFR 261.4') and section lead-in actor context ('A person who generates a solid waste'). Claim C0005 extracts only the later permission sentence and restricts its scope to 'If the waste is listed', omitting the essential prerequisite that the waste is not already excluded under 261.4 as well as the generator qualification. This broadens the permission to admit cases the source excludes (such as filing a delisting petition for waste already excluded under 261.4 or by a non-generator). Thus, scope and summary are errors.
